subproblems.title: Small perturbations x + tZ(x) of the identity by a compactly supported C¹ field are bi-Lipschitz bijections with injective derivative (parent steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be of class C¹ with compact support. Then there is t₀ > 0 such that for every t ∈ ℝ with |t| < t₀ the map Φ_t(x) := x + tZ(x) satisfies: (i) Φ_t is bijective; (ii) its derivative DΦ_t(x) is an injective linear map for every x ∈ ℝ^P; (iii) there is Λ ≥ 0 such that Φ_t is Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, i.e. |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| and |a − b| ≤ Λ|Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| for all a, b ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Z : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 Z → HasCompactSupport Z → ∃ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < t₀ → Bijective (fun x => x + t • Z x) ∧ (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun x => x + t • Z x) x)) ∧ ∃ Λ : NNReal, LipschitzWith Λ (fun x => x + t • Z x) ∧ AntilipschitzWith Λ (fun x => x + t • Z x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent steps 1 (choice of t₀ = 1/(1 + sup‖DZ‖)) and 2 (Φ_t is a diffeomorphism, the two-sided bound (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b| ≤ |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ (1 + |t|Λ)|a − b|, injectivity, surjectivity by a contraction, invertibility of DΦ) of the supplied proof of codim1_minimizing_piece_area_comparison; Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.2 (chapter-02.txt lines 1162–1205: φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) is a 1:1 map of U for small |t|). Here Z is only assumed C¹ (the parent applies it to its C^∞ field Z).
Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm of ℝ^P and ‖·‖ the operator norm. Write Φ := Φ_t once t is fixed.

Proof.
1. (Bound on DZ.) Z is C¹, so x ↦ DZ(x) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Z vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport Z, hence DZ(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport Z (the derivative of a function that is locally constant zero). Thus x ↦ ‖DZ(x)‖ is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport Z, so it is bounded: L := sup_x ‖DZ(x)‖ ∈ [0, ∞) (if tsupport Z = ∅, L = 0).
2. (Z is L-Lipschitz.) Z is differentiable on the convex set ℝ^P with ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ L for all x, so by the mean value inequality |Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ L|a − b| for all a, b (Mathlib lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le).
3. (Choice of t₀.) Put t₀ := 1/(1 + L) > 0. Fix t ∈ ℝ with |t| < t₀ and put κ := |t|L. Then 0 ≤ κ ≤ |t|(1 + L) < 1.
4. (Two-sided bound.) For a, b ∈ ℝ^P, Φ(a) − Φ(b) = (a − b) + t(Z(a) − Z(b)) and |t(Z(a) − Z(b))| ≤ |t|L|a − b| = κ|a − b| by step 2. By the triangle inequality,
 (4.1) (1 − κ)|a − b| ≤ |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ (1 + κ)|a − b|.
5. (Lipschitz and antilipschitz.) Let Λ := max(1 + κ, (1 − κ)^{-1}), a nonnegative real number (1 − κ > 0). By the right half of (4.1), Φ is (1 + κ)-Lipschitz, hence Λ-Lipschitz. By the left half, |a − b| ≤ (1 − κ)^{-1}|Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ Λ|Φ(a) − Φ(b)|; in the extended-distance form used by AntilipschitzWith this reads edist a b ≤ Λ·edist(Φ a, Φ b). So Φ is Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, which is (iii).
6. (Injectivity.) If Φ(a) = Φ(b), the left half of (4.1) gives (1 − κ)|a − b| ≤ 0, so a = b because 1 − κ > 0.
7. (Surjectivity.) Fix y ∈ ℝ^P and define T(x) := y − tZ(x). By step 2, |T(a) − T(b)| = |t||Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ κ|a − b| with κ < 1, so T is a contraction of the complete metric space ℝ^P. By the Banach fixed point theorem (Mathlib ContractingWith.fixedPoint with ContractingWith.fixedPoint_isFixedPt) there is x with T(x) = x, i.e. x + tZ(x) = y, i.e. Φ(x) = y. With step 6, Φ is bijective, which is (i).
8. (Derivative.) Φ is differentiable everywhere with DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) (derivative of the identity plus a constant multiple of Z). If DΦ(x)v = 0 then v = −tDZ(x)v, so |v| ≤ |t|‖DZ(x)‖|v| ≤ κ|v|; since κ < 1 this forces |v| = 0. Hence DΦ(x) is injective for every x, which is (ii).
9. (Conclusion.) Steps 5–8 hold for every t with |t| < t₀, and t₀ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: L := sup‖DZ‖ < ∞ since DZ is continuous and vanishes off the compact tsupport Z; Z is L-Lipschitz by the mean value inequality.
Λ := max(1 + κ, (1 − κ)^{-1}) makes Φ Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz; injectivity follows.
Surjectivity: the Banach fixed point of the contraction x ↦ y − tZ(x) solves Φ(x) = y.
DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) with ‖tDZ(x)‖ ≤ κ < 1 is injective.

subproblems.title: The image of an embedded C¹ submanifold under an antilipschitz C¹ bijection of ℝ^P with injective derivative is an embedded C¹ submanifold with tangent spaces DΦ(T_xN)
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold in the sense of Simon Ch. 2, 4.1 (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N), and let Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a C¹ bijection such that DΦ(x) is injective for every x and Φ is Λ-antilipschitz for some Λ ≥ 0 (|a − b| ≤ Λ|Φ(a) − Φ(b)|). Then Φ(N) is an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold, and for every x ∈ N the tangent space of Φ(N) at Φ(x) (contract tangentSpace: velocities γ′(0) of C¹ curves γ : (−1, 1) → Φ(N) with γ(0) = Φ(x)) is the image DΦ(x)(T_xN) of the tangent space of N at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → Bijective Φ → (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ x)) → AntilipschitzWith Λ Φ → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d (Φ '' N) ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, tangentSpace (Φ '' N) (Φ x) = (fderiv ℝ Φ x) '' tangentSpace N x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, §4, 4.1–4.3 (chapter-02.txt lines 846–875: local representations ψ : V → W with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ proper, Dψ of rank n; T_yM has basis D_1ψ(x), …, D_nψ(x)). It supplies the fact used in parent step 6 that Φ(M ∩ W) is a piece of the C¹ submanifold Φ(M) with tangent planes DΦ(x)(T_xM). Uses the sibling chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): for a local representation (V, W, ψ) of a set N (V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ C^r on V with r ≥ 1, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, Dψ injective on V) and v ∈ V, tangentSpace N (ψ(v)) = range Dψ(v).

Proof.
1. (Φ is a homeomorphism.) Φ is continuous, being C¹. Let Φ^{-1} be the inverse of the bijection Φ. For a, b ∈ ℝ^P, antilipschitzness applied to Φ^{-1}(a), Φ^{-1}(b) gives |Φ^{-1}(a) − Φ^{-1}(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b|, so Φ^{-1} is Lipschitz, hence continuous. Consequently Φ(O) = (Φ^{-1})^{-1}(O) is open for every open O, and Φ^{-1}(K) = Φ^{-1}''K is compact for every compact K (continuous image of a compact set).
2. (Charts of Φ(N).) Let y′ ∈ Φ(N), say y′ = Φ(y) with y ∈ N. By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N at y there are open V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P such that ψ is C¹ on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V. Put W′ := Φ(W) and ψ′ := Φ ∘ ψ. We verify the defining conditions for (V, W′, ψ′) at y′:
 (a) V is open; W′ is open by step 1; y′ = Φ(y) ∈ Φ(W) = W′.
 (b) ψ′ is C¹ on V: Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P and ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn).
 (c) ψ′ is injective on V: ψ is injective on V and Φ is injective.
 (d) ψ′(V) = Φ(ψ(V)) = Φ(W ∩ N) = Φ(W) ∩ Φ(N) = W′ ∩ Φ(N); the third equality holds because Φ is injective (Set.image_inter).
 (e) Properness: let K ⊆ W′ be compact. Then K′ := Φ^{-1}(K) is compact (step 1), and K′ ⊆ W: if Φ(z) ∈ K ⊆ Φ(W), then Φ(z) = Φ(w) for some w ∈ W and z = w by injectivity. Since V ∩ ψ′^{-1}(K) = V ∩ ψ^{-1}(Φ^{-1}(K)) = V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K′), it is compact by the properness of ψ.
 (f) Let z ∈ V. As V is open and ψ is C¹ on V, ψ is differentiable at z; Φ is differentiable at ψ(z). By the chain rule Dψ′(z) = DΦ(ψ(z)) ∘ Dψ(z), a composition of two injective linear maps, hence injective.
 Since y′ ∈ Φ(N) was arbitrary, Φ(N) is an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d (Φ '' N)).
3. (Tangent spaces.) Let x ∈ N. Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at x as in step 2, and v ∈ V with ψ(v) = x (possible since x ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V)). By chart_tangent_space (with r = 1) applied to N and (V, W, ψ): T_xN = range Dψ(v). By step 2 (a)–(f), (V, W′, ψ′) satisfies all hypotheses of chart_tangent_space for the set Φ(N), and ψ′(v) = Φ(x); hence
 T_{Φ(x)}Φ(N) = range Dψ′(v) = range(DΦ(x) ∘ Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(T_xN).
 This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz + bijective + continuous: Φ is a homeomorphism (Φ^{-1} is Λ-Lipschitz).
For a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at y, (V, Φ(W), Φ∘ψ) is a chart of Φ(N) at Φ(y): open, C¹, injective, image Φ(W) ∩ Φ(N), proper via Φ^{-1}(K) compact, injective derivative by the chain rule.
chart_tangent_space for both charts: T_{Φ(x)}Φ(N) = range D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(x)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(T_xN).

Notation. |·| Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ operator norm, B_ρ(z) open ball, B̄_ρ(z) closed ball, L^m Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m (= μHE[m] on Euclid m, Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For a linear map L : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, J(L) := normDet(L) = (det(LᵀL))^{1/2} (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet; Simon 3.3); L ↦ J(L) is continuous (SimonGMT Chapter02 continuous_normDet). η_{x,r} = SimonGMT blowUpMap x r.
Area formula (Simon 3.2; SimonGMT Chapter02 injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative): if D ⊆ ℝ^m is open, F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is C¹ on D, injective on D, with DF(u) injective for u ∈ D, then H^m(F(A)) = ∫_A J(DF(u)) du for every Borel A ⊆ D. Since F(D ∩ F^{-1}(E)) = F(D) ∩ E, this says that the Borel measures E ↦ H^m(F(G) ∩ E) and E ↦ ∫_{G ∩ F^{-1}(E)} J(DF) du agree for every Borel G ⊆ D, i.e. H^m⌞F(G) is the image of J(DF)·L^m⌞G under F (in Lean, Measure.map F (…) with the a.e.-measurability of F on G supplied by ContinuousOn.aemeasurable, since Measure.map of a non-a.e.-measurable map is 0; F(A) is Borel for Borel A ⊆ D by MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn); hence (★) ∫_{F(G)} g dH^m = ∫_G g(F(u)) J(DF(u)) du for every bounded Borel g : ℝ^P → ℝ when the right side has an integrable bound (apply the measure identity to g⁺ and g⁻).

Proof.
1. (Chart; dimension of Q.) By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N at x there are open V ⊆ ℝ^m, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W₀ and ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, C¹ on V, injective on V, with ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀, and Dψ(v) injective for v ∈ V. Choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x and put A := Dψ(v₀). By chart_tangent_space, T_xN = range A; hence Q = range A as subspaces (equal underlying sets). A is injective, so dim Q = m: the first conjunct.
2. (Uniform bounds near v₀.) As m ≥ 1 and A is injective, c₀ := min_{|u|=1}|Au| > 0 (the unit sphere of ℝ^m is compact and nonempty), and |Au| ≥ c₀|u| for all u. By continuity of Dψ at v₀ (ψ is C¹ on the open set V) choose ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dψ(v) − A‖ ≤ c₀/2 for v ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀). The mean value inequality for v ↦ ψ(v) − Av on the convex set B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀) gives |ψ(v) − ψ(v′) − A(v − v′)| ≤ (c₀/2)|v − v′|, hence
 (2.1) |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ (c₀/2)|v − v′| for v, v′ ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀).
 Moreover v ↦ J(Dψ(v)) is continuous on the compact set B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀), so C_J := max_{B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀)} J(Dψ) < ∞.
3. (Localization.) Choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀. The set C₁ := (V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B̄_ε(x))) ∖ B_{ρ₀}(v₀) is compact (a closed subset of the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B̄_ε(x)), properness), so ψ(C₁) is compact (ψ is continuous on V ⊇ C₁). x ∉ ψ(C₁), since ψ(v) = x = ψ(v₀) with v ∈ V forces v = v₀ ∈ B_{ρ₀}(v₀). Let δ := min(ε, dist(x, ψ(C₁))) > 0 (δ := ε if C₁ = ∅). Then
 (3.1) N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) and N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ N ∩ W.
 Indeed let y ∈ N with |y − x| < δ ≤ ε; then y ∈ W ∩ W₀ ∩ N, so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ε(x); if v ∉ B_{ρ₀}(v₀) then v ∈ C₁ and |y − x| ≥ dist(x, ψ(C₁)) ≥ δ, a contradiction.
4. (Reduction to the chart.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0). Let 0 < r < δ/R. Put G_r := B_{ρ₀/r}(0) ⊆ ℝ^m (so v₀ + ru ∈ B_{ρ₀}(v₀) for u ∈ G_r), ψ_r(u) := r^{-1}(ψ(v₀ + ru) − x), and G′_r := {u ∈ G_r : |ψ_r(u)| < R}, an open set (ψ_r is continuous on the open set G_r). Then
 (4.1) η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) ∩ B_R(0) = ψ_r(G′_r).
 ⊇: for u ∈ G′_r, y := ψ(v₀ + ru) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N, and |y − x| = r|ψ_r(u)| < rR < δ ≤ ε, so y ∈ W; thus ψ_r(u) = η_{x,r}(y) ∈ η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) ∩ B_R(0). ⊆: if y ∈ N ∩ W and |η_{x,r}(y)| < R, then |y − x| < rR < δ, so by (3.1) y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B_{ρ₀}(v₀); u := (v − v₀)/r ∈ G_r and ψ_r(u) = η_{x,r}(y), so u ∈ G′_r.
 N is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_of_isSimonSubmanifold, after unfolding the contract's chart conditions into IsSimonSubmanifold), W is open and η_{x,r} is a homeomorphism, so η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) is Borel. Since f vanishes outside B_R(0), Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero and (4.1) give
 (4.2) ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f dH^m = ∫_{ψ_r(G′_r)} f dH^m.
5. (Area formula in the chart.) ψ_r is C¹ on the open set G_r, injective there (ψ is injective on V), and Dψ_r(u) = Dψ(v₀ + ru) (chain rule) is injective. By (2.1), for u ∈ G′_r: R > |ψ_r(u)| = r^{-1}|ψ(v₀ + ru) − ψ(v₀)| ≥ (c₀/2)|u|, so G′_r ⊆ B_{2R/c₀}(0), and J(Dψ_r(u)) ≤ C_J. Hence (★) applies to F = ψ_r, G = G′_r and g = f, and since f(ψ_r(u)) = 0 for u ∈ G_r ∖ G′_r:
 (5.1) ∫_{ψ_r(G′_r)} f dH^m = ∫_{G′_r} f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) du = ∫_{ℝ^m} h_r(u) du, h_r(u) := 1_{G_r}(u) f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)).
6. (Domination.) If h_r(u) ≠ 0 then u ∈ G′_r, so |u| < 2R/c₀ (step 5). Hence |h_r(u)| ≤ H(u) := sup|f|·C_J·1_{B_{2R/c₀}(0)}(u) for all u and all r ∈ (0, δ/R); H is integrable and independent of r. Each h_r is measurable (indicator of the open set G_r times a function continuous on G_r).
7. (Pointwise limit.) Fix u ∈ ℝ^m. For r < ρ₀/(|u| + 1) we have u ∈ G_r. As r ↓ 0: ψ_r(u) = r^{-1}(ψ(v₀ + ru) − ψ(v₀)) → Au (differentiability of ψ at v₀), so f(ψ_r(u)) → f(Au) by continuity of f; and Dψ(v₀ + ru) → A (continuity of Dψ at v₀), so J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) → J(A) by continuity of J. Hence h_r(u) → J(A) f(Au).
8. (Dominated convergence.) The filter r ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated; by steps 6–7 and the dominated convergence theorem (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ h_r du → J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du. By (4.2) and (5.1), lim_{r↓0} ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f dH^m = J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du.
9. (The plane.) For the injective linear map A, H^m(A(S)) = J(A)·L^m(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^m (Simon 3.1; Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume). As A is injective, A(A^{-1}(E)) = range A ∩ E, so H^m⌞range A is the image of J(A)·L^m under A, and ∫_{range A} f dH^m = J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du (f is continuous with compact support, so all integrals are finite). Since range A = Q (step 1), step 8 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0.
10. (Conclusion.) Steps 1 and 9 (f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) arbitrary) are the two conjuncts of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (N ∩ W) x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Chart (V, W₀, ψ) at x = ψ(v₀); chart_tangent_space gives Q = range Dψ(v₀) = range A, so dim Q = m.
Near v₀: |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ (c₀/2)|v − v′| with c₀ = min_{|u|=1}|Au| > 0, and J(Dψ) ≤ C_J.
Properness and injectivity give δ > 0 with N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) ∩ W.
For f supported in B_R(0) and r < δ/R, ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f = ∫ 1_{G_r}(u) f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) du with ψ_r(u) = r^{-1}(ψ(v₀ + ru) − x) (area formula).
Dominated by sup|f|·C_J·1_{B_{2R/c₀}(0)}; pointwise limit J(A) f(Au); dominated convergence.
Linear area formula: J(A)∫ f(Au) du = ∫_{range A} f dH^m = ∫_Q f dH^m.

subproblems.title: Area formula for an injective C¹ immersion of ℝ^P restricted to an embedded C¹ submanifold, and continuity of its tangential Jacobian (Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded m-dimensional C¹ submanifold, Q : ℝ^P → {linear subspaces of ℝ^P} with Q(x) = T_xN (as sets) for every x ∈ N, and Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ injective map with DΦ(x) injective for every x. Let J(x) := (det(⟨DΦ(x)e_i(x), DΦ(x)e_j(x)⟩)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where e(x) = (e_i(x))_{i < dim Q(x)} is the standard orthonormal basis of Q(x) (stdOrthonormalBasis). Then J is continuous on N, and for every Borel set B ⊆ N and every function g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫_{Φ(B)} g dH^m = ∫_B J(x) g(Φ(x)) dH^m(x) (lower Lebesgue integrals, H^m = μHE[m]).

This is the area formula invoked in parent step 6 ("Area formula for the injective C¹ map Φ on the C¹ submanifold M"). SimonGMT's IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Euclid m) 1 N follows from IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N by reordering the chart conditions (the smoothness exponent (1 : ℕ) casts to (1 : ℕ∞), and the properness condition has its arguments permuted); this node's own Lean proof performs exactly this conversion for M.
Notation. For a linear map L : U → ℝ^P on a finite-dimensional inner product space U, normDet(L) ≥ 0 is the Mathlib LinearMap.normDet: normDet(L)² = det(⟨Lb_i, Lb_j⟩) for every orthonormal basis b of U (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram); normDet(L) > 0 iff L is injective; normDet(g∘f) = normDet(g|_{range f})·normDet(f) (LinearMap.normDet_comp); L ↦ normDet(L) is continuous on maps ℝ^m → ℝ^P (SimonGMT Chapter02 continuous_normDet). L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m (= μHE[m] there).

Proof.
1. (J is a norm determinant.) For x ∈ ℝ^P let L_x : Q(x) → ℝ^P be the restriction of DΦ(x). Applying normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the orthonormal basis e(x) of Q(x): J(x)² = det(⟨DΦ(x)e_i(x), DΦ(x)e_j(x)⟩) = normDet(L_x)², and both J(x) and normDet(L_x) are ≥ 0, so J(x) = normDet(L_x). In particular J(x) depends only on DΦ(x) and the subspace Q(x), and J(x) > 0 because L_x is injective.
2. (Chart formula.) Let (V, W₀, ψ) be a local representation of N (V ⊆ ℝ^m open, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ C¹ on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, proper, Dψ injective on V) and v ∈ V. By chart_tangent_space, Q(ψ(v)) = T_{ψ(v)}N = range Dψ(v). By the chain rule D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(ψ(v))∘Dψ(v), and by normDet_comp and step 1 (the restriction of DΦ(ψ(v)) to range Dψ(v) = Q(ψ(v)) is L_{ψ(v)}):
 (2.1) normDet(D(Φ∘ψ)(v)) = J(ψ(v))·normDet(Dψ(v)), with normDet(Dψ(v)) > 0.
3. (ψ is a homeomorphism onto W₀ ∩ N; Simon 4.2.) ψ maps V continuously and bijectively onto W₀ ∩ N. It is relatively closed: let F ⊆ V be closed in V and y_j = ψ(v_j) → y ∈ W₀ ∩ N with v_j ∈ F. The set K := {y} ∪ {y_j : j ≥ j₀} is compact and, for j₀ large, contained in W₀ (W₀ is an open neighbourhood of y), so the v_j (j ≥ j₀) lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K); a subsequence converges to some v ∈ V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K), v ∈ F as F is closed in V, and ψ(v) = y. Hence ψ(F) is closed in W₀ ∩ N, and ψ^{-1} : W₀ ∩ N → V is continuous. (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isEmbedding_chartMap.)
4. (Continuity of J on N.) On V the maps v ↦ Dψ(v) and v ↦ DΦ(ψ(v)) are continuous (ψ is C¹ on the open set V, Φ is C¹), hence so is v ↦ D(Φ∘ψ)(v), and normDet is continuous. By (2.1), J∘ψ = normDet(D(Φ∘ψ))/normDet(Dψ) is continuous on V. By step 3, J = (J∘ψ)∘ψ^{-1} is continuous on W₀ ∩ N. W₀ ∩ N is a neighbourhood of each of its points relative to N (W₀ is open), so J is continuous within N at each point of W₀ ∩ N. The charts cover N, so J is continuous on N: the first conclusion.
5. (Φ is a measurable embedding.) Φ is continuous and injective on the Polish space ℝ^P, so by the Lusin–Souslin theorem it is a measurable embedding (Mathlib Continuous.measurableEmbedding): Φ(E) is Borel for Borel E, and ∫ g d(Φ_*μ) = ∫ g∘Φ dμ for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and every measure μ (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). (Alternatively: DΦ(x) is invertible for every x, so Φ is an open map by the inverse function theorem and a homeomorphism onto its open image.)
6. (N is Borel.) N is covered by countably many chart sets W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V) (Lindelöf, ℝ^P second countable), each σ-compact (V is σ-compact and ψ continuous on V), so N is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_of_isSimonSubmanifold, after unfolding the contract's chart conditions into IsSimonSubmanifold). By step 4, J·1_N is Borel; in particular J is a.e.-measurable for H^m⌞B whenever B ⊆ N is Borel.
7. (Set formula in a chart.) Let (V, W₀, ψ) be a chart and A ⊆ V Borel. ψ and Φ∘ψ are injective on A, differentiable within A, with injective derivatives. By the parametric area formula (Simon 3.2; SimonGMT Chapter02 injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative) and (2.1):
 (7.1) H^m(ψ(A)) = ∫_A normDet(Dψ(v)) dv,
 (7.2) H^m(Φ(ψ(A))) = ∫_A normDet(D(Φ∘ψ)(v)) dv = ∫_A J(ψ(v)) normDet(Dψ(v)) dv.
 Formula (7.1) for all Borel A ⊆ V says (as ψ(V ∩ ψ^{-1}(E)) = ψ(V) ∩ E, and V ∩ ψ^{-1}(E) is Borel for Borel E) that H^m⌞ψ(V) is the image of normDet(Dψ)·L^m⌞V under ψ (in Lean, Measure.map ψ (…) with the a.e.-measurability of ψ on V supplied by ContinuousOn.aemeasurable — Measure.map of a non-a.e.-measurable map is 0 — and ψ(A) Borel by MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). Integrating the H^m⌞ψ(V)-measurable function 1_{ψ(A)}·J (step 6) against this measure gives ∫_{ψ(A)} J dH^m = ∫_A J(ψ(v)) normDet(Dψ(v)) dv. Comparing with (7.2): H^m(Φ(B)) = ∫_B J dH^m for every Borel B ⊆ W₀ ∩ N (take A := V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B), so ψ(A) = B).
8. (Set formula on N.) Choose charts (V_k, W_k, ψ_k), k ∈ ℕ, whose sets W_k cover N (step 6). For a Borel B ⊆ N let B_k := (B ∩ W_k) ∖ ⋃_{i<k} W_i: Borel, pairwise disjoint, with union B, and B_k ⊆ W_k ∩ N. Since Φ is injective, the Borel sets Φ(B_k) are pairwise disjoint with union Φ(B). By step 7 and countable additivity:
 (8.1) H^m(Φ(B)) = Σ_k H^m(Φ(B_k)) = Σ_k ∫_{B_k} J dH^m = ∫_B J dH^m for every Borel B ⊆ N.
9. (Function formula.) Fix a Borel B ⊆ N. Let ν₁ := H^m⌞Φ(B) and ν₂ := Φ_*(J·(H^m⌞B)), where J·μ denotes the measure with density ofReal∘J. For Borel E, Φ(B) ∩ E = Φ(B ∩ Φ^{-1}(E)) (Φ injective) and B ∩ Φ^{-1}(E) is a Borel subset of N, so by (8.1) ν₁(E) = ∫_{B∩Φ^{-1}(E)} J dH^m = ν₂(E). Hence ν₁ = ν₂, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]:
 ∫_{Φ(B)} g dH^m = ∫ g dν₁ = ∫ g dν₂ = ∫_B J·(g∘Φ) dH^m,
 using step 5 (integration against an image measure by a measurable embedding, valid for every g) and ∫ h d(J·μ) = ∫ J·h dμ for every h ≥ 0 when J is a.e.-measurable and finite (Mathlib lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable₀; step 6). With ofReal(J(x)) in place of J(x) this is the asserted identity ∫⁻_{Φ(B)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(x))·g(Φ(x)) dH^m(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: J(x) = normDet(DΦ(x)|_{Q(x)}) > 0 (Gram determinant in an orthonormal basis).
In a chart: Q(ψ(v)) = range Dψ(v) (chart_tangent_space) and normDet(D(Φ∘ψ)(v)) = J(ψ(v))·normDet(Dψ(v)) (normDet_comp).
Charts are homeomorphisms onto W₀ ∩ N (properness), so J = normDet(D(Φ∘ψ))/normDet(Dψ)∘ψ^{-1} is continuous on N.
Parametric area formula for ψ and Φ∘ψ gives H^m(Φ(B)) = ∫_B J dH^m for Borel B in a chart; countable chart cover and injectivity extend it to Borel B ⊆ N.
Hence H^m⌞Φ(B) = Φ_*(J·H^m⌞B); integrating g (Φ a measurable embedding, J a.e.-measurable) gives ∫_{Φ(B)} g = ∫_B J g∘Φ.

subproblems.title: The push-forward of an oriented multiplicity-one C¹ piece by a bi-Lipschitz C¹ bijection with injective derivative is an integer multiplicity current of mass at most the area of the image (Simon 6.2.24(3), 6.3.9 for C¹ pieces)

1. Bound on Dφ. K is compact, hence closed, and φ = id on the open set E ∖ K, so Dφ(x) = I for x ∉ K (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Dφ is continuous (φ is C¹, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), hence ‖Dφ‖ ≤ c on K for some c ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). So with Λ := max(1, c), ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ E.

By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q, an orthonormal τ : Fin n → E and a sign with ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) for all n-covectors β; since |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ ∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all β, for μ-a.e. x. subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^P, K' ⊆ E compact, ψ : E → E a C^∞ map with ψ(x) = x for every x ∉ K', and α a test d-form on E (C^∞ with compact support; IsTestForm α). Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the pull-back ψ^#ω of a test form under a smooth map, Simon 6.2.23–6.2.24), with details filled in.

Notation:
- E := ℝ^P.
- For L ∈ E →L[ℝ] E, Φ(L) := ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L, the continuous linear map γ ↦ γ∘L on d-covectors. Thus (ψ^#α)(x) = Φ(Dψ(x))(α(ψ(x))) by compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply.
- F₀ := tsupport α ∪ K'.

1. Properties of α. IsTestForm α = IsSmoothForm α ∧ HasCompactSupport α, and IsSmoothForm α means ContDiff ℝ ∞ α. So α is C^∞ and tsupport α is compact.

2. Smoothness of ψ^#α.
 (a) Φ is analytic on all of E →L[ℝ] E (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM univ), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
 (b) Since ψ is C^∞, x ↦ Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right with m = ∞, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
 (c) x ↦ α(ψ(x)) is C^∞, as the composition of the C^∞ maps α (step 1) and ψ (ContDiff.comp).
 (d) By (a) and (b), x ↦ Φ(Dψ(x)) is a C^∞ map into the continuous linear maps on d-covectors. Applying a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to the C^∞ family of vectors in (c) is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply).
 Hence x ↦ Φ(Dψ(x))(α(ψ(x))) = (ψ^#α)(x) is C^∞, i.e. IsSmoothForm (ψ^#α) (unfold IsSmoothForm to ContDiff ℝ ∞).

3. F₀ is closed. tsupport α is closed by definition. K' is compact in the Hausdorff space E, hence closed. A union of two closed sets is closed.

4. ψ^#α vanishes off F₀. Let z ∉ F₀.
 - Then z ∉ K', so ψ(z) = z by hypothesis.
 - Also z ∉ tsupport α, so α(z) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
 - Hence (ψ^#α)(z) = α(z)∘Dψ(z) = 0∘Dψ(z) = 0, since the zero d-covector composed with any linear map is zero (both sides give 0 on every d-tuple of vectors).
 Thus support(ψ^#α) ⊆ F₀.

5. Support bound. By steps 3 and 4, tsupport(ψ^#α) = closure(support(ψ^#α)) ⊆ F₀ = tsupport α ∪ K' (closure_minimal). This is the second conjunct.

6. Compact support. tsupport α is compact (step 1) and K' is compact, so F₀ is compact. tsupport(ψ^#α) is closed and contained in F₀ (step 5), hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport (ψ^#α).

7. Conclusion. Steps 2 and 6 give IsTestForm (ψ^#α) = IsSmoothForm (ψ^#α) ∧ HasCompactSupport (ψ^#α), the first conjunct. Step 5 is the second conjunct.

ψ^#α(x) = Φ(Dψ(x))(α(ψ(x))) where Φ(L) = compContinuousLinearMapCLM L is analytic, hence C^∞. Since Dψ and α∘ψ are also C^∞, ψ^#α is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply).
F₀ = tsupport α ∪ K' is closed (K' is compact in a Hausdorff space) and compact.
For z ∉ F₀, ψ(z) = z and α(z) = 0, so ψ^#α(z) = 0. Since F₀ is closed, tsupport ψ^#α ⊆ F₀.
tsupport ψ^#α is a closed subset of the compact set F₀, so ψ^#α has compact support and is a test form.

subproblems.title: Differences of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1))
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity currents. Then S − T is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (S - T)

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof), used in the parent proof step 5 ('S + T₂ is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.2(1))'). Uses the sibling approx_tangent_locality and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Notation: ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); a unit orientation of a subspace Q is ±ev_τ with τ an orthonormal basis of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf); for such ξ', |ξ'(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm), and ξ' ≠ 0 since ξ'(±β_τ) = 1 for β_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩).

1. (Data.) Let R_S = (C_S, θ_S, ξ_S) represent S and R_T = (C_T, θ_T, ξ_T) represent T. Then C := C_S ∪ C_T is Borel, ⊆ U, countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and for compact K ⊆ U, H^n(C ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{C_S∩K} θ_S dH^n + ∫_{C_T∩K} θ_T dH^n < ∞, as θ_S, θ_T ≥ 1 on their carriers.

2. (Common tangent planes on the overlap.) By approx_tangent_locality applied to C_S ⊆ C and to C_T ⊆ C: for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C_S x Q for all Q, and likewise for C_T. Together with the orientation conditions of R_S and R_T and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T the approximate tangent space Q_x of C at x exists and ξ_S(x), ξ_T(x) are both unit orientations of Q_x.

3. (Sign lemma.) If τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q, then α(τ') = det(B) α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n, where B_{ij} := ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, and det B = ±1. Indeed τ'_j = Σ_i B_{ij} τ_i; expanding multilinearly and using that α is alternating, α(τ') = Σ_{σ∈Sym(n)} sgn(σ) ∏_j B_{σ(j) j} · α(τ) = det(B) α(τ); and BᵀB = (⟨τ'_i, τ'_j⟩) = I, so det(B)² = 1. Consequently, by step 2, ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T.

4. (Measurable bookkeeping.) Let ξ̃_S, ξ̃_T be Borel functions with ξ̃_S = ξ_S H^n-a.e. on C_S and ξ̃_T = ξ_T H^n-a.e. on C_T. Let σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃_T(x) = ξ̃_S(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). Then ξ_T = σ ξ_S H^n-a.e. on C_S ∩ C_T: at a.e. such x, ξ̃_S(x) = ξ_S(x), ξ̃_T(x) = ξ_T(x) and ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x) (step 3); if ξ_T(x) = ξ_S(x) then σ(x) = 1, and otherwise ξ_T(x) = −ξ_S(x) and σ(x) = −1. For x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T let d(x) := θ_S(x) − σ(x) θ_T(x) ∈ ℤ. Define
 C' := (C_S ∖ C_T) ∪ (C_T ∖ C_S) ∪ {x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T : d(x) ≠ 0} (Borel);
 θ'(x) := θ_S(x) on C_S ∖ C_T, θ_T(x) on C_T ∖ C_S, |d(x)| on C_S ∩ C_T, and 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued, ≥ 1 on C');
 ξ'(x) := ξ_S(x) on C_S ∖ C_T, −ξ_T(x) on C_T ∖ C_S, sign(d(x)) ξ_S(x) on C_S ∩ C_T (a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C').

5. (R' := (C', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U.) C' ⊆ C ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (subset of C). θ' ≤ θ_S + θ_T on C', so ∫_{C'∩K} θ' dH^n < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Orientation: C' is the union of the Borel pieces P₁ := C_S ∖ C_T ⊆ C_S, P₂ := C_T ∖ C_S ⊆ C_T and P₃ := C' ∩ C_S ∩ C_T ⊆ C_S. For P₁, apply approx_tangent_locality to P₁ ⊆ C_S and to P₁ ⊆ C' (H^n(C' ∩ K) ≤ H^n(C ∩ K) < ∞): for H^n-a.e. x ∈ P₁ the approximate tangent spaces of C_S, P₁ and C' at x coincide, and ξ'(x) = ξ_S(x) is a unit orientation of the one of C_S. Similarly for P₂ (with C_T and −ξ_T; −ev_τ is again a unit orientation, the definition allowing either sign) and for P₃ (with C_S and sign(d) ξ_S). Hence for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C' there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C' x Q and ξ'(x) a unit orientation of Q.

6. (R' represents S − T.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). The functions θ_S ξ_S(ω) and θ_T ξ_T(ω) are bounded by θ_S ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, resp. θ_T ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, a.e. on their carriers, hence integrable, and (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{C_S} θ_S ξ_S(ω) dH^n − ∫_{C_T} θ_T ξ_T(ω) dH^n. Split both integrals over C_S ∖ C_T, C_T ∖ C_S and C_S ∩ C_T. On C_S ∩ C_T the combined integrand is a.e. θ_S ξ_S(ω) − θ_T σ ξ_S(ω) = d ξ_S(ω) = |d| sign(d) ξ_S(ω), which vanishes where d = 0. Therefore (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{C'} θ' ξ'(ω) dH^n = R'.action ω for every ω, so R' represents S − T and S − T is integer multiplicity.
proof_key_steps: On C_S ∩ C_T both orientations orient the common approximate tangent plane of C_S ∪ C_T (locality), so ξ_T = ±ξ_S there (an orthonormal change of frame has determinant ±1).
Carrier C' = (C_S △ C_T) ∪ {d ≠ 0}, multiplicity |θ_S − σθ_T| on the overlap, orientation sign(d)ξ_S; locality transfers the orientation condition to C'.
Splitting the integrals over the three pieces shows that R' represents S − T.

Source: step 8 of the parent proof; Simon 6.3.4–3.5 and 3.7 (chapter-06.txt lines 787–831: df_x#ξ = ±D_{τ_1}f ∧ ⋯ ∧ D_{τ_n}f = det(D_{τ_i}f · η_j) η_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ η_n, J^M_f = |det(D_{τ_i}f · η_j)|, so df_x#ξ = J^M_f η with η = ±η_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ η_n), with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; for an n-covector β, β∘L := β.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (ξ.comp (compContinuousLinearMapCLM L))(β) = ξ(β∘L) =: ζ(β), and (β∘L)(w) = β(Lw₁, …, Lw_n); for vectors w = (w₁, …, w_n), G(w) := (⟨w_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}.
1. Data. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → E with span τ = Q and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = s β(τ) for all β. τ is a basis of Q, so dim Q = n, and e := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q is indexed by Fin (dim Q) = Fin n (reindex along dim Q = n; the determinant is invariant under this reindexing).
2. Basis independence. e and τ are orthonormal bases of Q, so e_b = Σ_a O_{ab} τ_a with O an orthogonal n×n matrix. Then G(Le) = Oᵀ G(Lτ) O, so det G(Le) = det(O)² det G(Lτ) = det G(Lτ), and J = sqrt(det G(Lτ)). (Alternatively both determinants equal normDet(L|_Q)², Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram.)
3. Gram–Schmidt. v_a := Lτ_a (a = 1, …, n) are linearly independent (L injective, τ independent), and span v = L(span τ) = L(Q) = Submodule.map L Q. Let σ be the orthonormal basis of L(Q) obtained by Gram–Schmidt from v (Mathlib gramSchmidtNormed / gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis), and A_{ab} := ⟨v_b, σ_a⟩, so v_b = Σ_a A_{ab} σ_a; for Gram–Schmidt A is upper triangular (σ_a ∈ span(v_1, …, v_a)). A is invertible because v is a basis of L(Q).
4. Determinants. By orthonormality of σ, ⟨v_a, v_b⟩ = Σ_c A_{ca}A_{cb}, i.e. G(Lτ) = AᵀA, so det G(Lτ) = det(A)² and J = |det A| > 0. For every n-covector β, β(v) = det(A) β(σ): the restriction of β to the n-dimensional space L(Q) is an alternating n-form, hence equals β(σ)·det_σ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det), and det_σ(v) = det A (Basis.det_apply: the matrix of v in the basis σ is A).
5. Bound. As A is upper triangular, det A = Π_a A_{aa} and |A_{aa}| = |⟨v_a, σ_a⟩| ≤ |v_a| = |Lτ_a| ≤ ‖L‖, so J = Π_a |A_{aa}| ≤ ‖L‖^n. (Equivalently, Hadamard's inequality det G(v) ≤ Π_a |v_a|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2n}.)
6. Orientation. For every β: ζ(β) = ξ(β∘L) = s (β∘L)(τ) = s β(Lτ) = s β(v) = s det(A) β(σ). Hence (J^{-1}ζ)(β) = s·sign(det A)·β(σ) with s·sign(det A) ∈ {1, −1}; σ is orthonormal with span σ = L(Q). So IsUnitOrientationOf (J^{-1}ζ) (L(Q)) holds, with the same orthonormal family σ and the same sign for every β.
7. The case n = 0 is included: τ, σ, A are empty, Q = L(Q) = {0}, the determinant of the empty matrix is 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty), J = 1 ∈ (0, ‖L‖^0], β∘L = β for every 0-covector β (it takes no arguments), so J^{-1}ζ = ξ, which orients {0} = L(Q) with the same sign. (Imports: gramSchmidtNormed lives in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.GramSchmidtOrtho and normDet in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet; the submission may import them, the frozen statement does not use them.)
proof_key_steps: Write ξ = s·(evaluation at τ) with τ an orthonormal basis of Q; dim Q = n.
The Gram determinant of L on Q does not depend on the orthonormal basis, so J = sqrt(det G(Lτ)).

|A_aa| ≤ |Lτ_a| ≤ ‖L‖ gives J ≤ ‖L‖^n.

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, §1: coordinate covectors dx^I and the pairing of Λⁿ with Λₙ). The Cauchy–Binet identity is proved inline.
Notation:
- e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun), and v(i) is the i-th coordinate of v ∈ ℝ^P.
- Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ; Λₙ := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ.
- 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
- For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. The defining sum runs over all I : Fin n → Fin P, with term α(e_I)² for strictly increasing I and 0 otherwise, so it is the same sum.
- For v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and I ∈ 𝓘, v^I is the n×n matrix with (k, j) entry v_j(I(k)).
1. (Coordinate covectors.) For I ∈ 𝓘 let dx^I ∈ Λⁿ be dx^I(v) := det(v^I). It is n-linear and alternating in v, because the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its columns and column j, (v_j(I(k)))_k, depends linearly on v_j. It is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. In SimonGMT (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality), dx^I = wedgeCovectors n (fun k ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I k)), and wedgeCovectors_apply_det gives exactly this formula. For n = 0, dx^I is the constant covector 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
2. (Kronecker property.) For I, J ∈ 𝓘, dx^I(e_J) = 1 if I = J and dx^I(e_J) = 0 if I ≠ J. The matrix (e_J)^I has (k, j) entry 1 if I(k) = J(j) and 0 otherwise. If I = J it is the identity matrix. If I ≠ J, the ranges differ, because a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the increasing enumeration of its range. Both ranges have n elements, so some I(k) is not in range J. Row k of (e_J)^I is then zero, and the determinant is 0.
3. (Expansion.) For every α ∈ Λⁿ and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n: α(v) = Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I(v).
 Both sides are alternating n-linear functions of v; the right side is a linear combination of the dx^I. By multilinearity, two n-linear maps on ℝ^P agree once they agree on every basis tuple e_f := (e_{f(0)}, …, e_{f(n−1)}), f : Fin n → Fin P.
 - If f is not injective, both alternating maps vanish at e_f, which has a repeated entry.
 - If f is injective, let J ∈ 𝓘 enumerate range f increasingly, and let σ be the permutation of Fin n with f = J ∘ σ. By alternation, each side at e_f equals sign(σ) times its value at e_J. At e_J the right side is Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I(e_J) = α(e_J) by step 2.
 Hence the two sides agree.
4. (Sum of squared minors; Cauchy–Binet.) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} det(τ^I)² = 1. This is the Cauchy–Binet formula det(AᵀA) = Σ_I det(A_I)² for the P×n matrix A with columns τ_j, where AᵀA = Id. Self-contained derivation:
 - Let δ_τ ∈ Λⁿ be δ_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear, alternating and continuous for the same reasons as dx^I, and equals wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ ⟨τ_i, ·⟩).
 - By orthonormality, δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det(Id) = 1.
 - δ_τ(e_I) = det(τ_i(I(j)))_{i,j} = det((τ^I)ᵀ) = det(τ^I), and dx^I(τ) = det(τ^I).
 - Step 3 with α = δ_τ and v = τ gives 1 = δ_τ(τ) = Σ_I δ_τ(e_I)·dx^I(τ) = Σ_I det(τ^I)².
5. (Proof of (a).) Let ξ, Q satisfy IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, with orthonormal τ and sign s, so ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. For α ∈ Λⁿ, step 3 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘 give
 |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| = |Σ_I α(e_I) det(τ^I)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I det(τ^I)²)^{1/2} = |α|·1,
 using step 4.
6. (Definition of L.) For ζ ∈ Λₙ put L(ζ) := Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^I)·dx^I. Each ζ ↦ ζ(dx^I) is evaluation at a fixed point, a continuous linear functional on Λₙ. So L is a finite sum of continuous linear maps Λₙ → Λⁿ, i.e. L ∈ (MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n). For example, L = Σ_I (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (dx^I)).smulRight (dx^I). L does not depend on ξ.
7. (Coefficients of L(ζ).) For J ∈ 𝓘, step 2 gives L(ζ)(e_J) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I(e_J) = ζ(dx^J). Hence |L(ζ)|² = Σ_{J ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^J)².
8. (Proof of (b) and (c).) For ξ as in step 5, ξ(dx^J) = s·dx^J(τ) = s·det(τ^J).
 - By step 7 and step 4, |L(ξ)|² = Σ_J s²·det(τ^J)² = 1, so |L(ξ)| = 1 ≤ 1.
 - By linearity of ξ, ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I ξ(dx^I)·ξ(dx^I) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.
9. (Degenerate cases need no separate treatment.)
 - For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map, e_∅ is the empty tuple, dx^∅ = 1 and |α| = |α(e_∅)|. Steps 1–8 hold verbatim.
 - If n > P, then 𝓘 = ∅ and step 4 would give 0 = 1. So ℝ^P has no orthonormal family of n vectors, the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q never holds, and the statement is vacuous (L = 0).
proof_key_steps: Define dx^I(v) = det(v_j(I(k)))_{k,j} (SimonGMT wedgeCovectors of coordinate projections); dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J.
Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·dx^I(v): both sides are alternating multilinear and agree on all basis tuples.
Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 for orthonormal τ (Cauchy–Binet), by expanding δ_τ(v) = det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩) at v = τ.
Cauchy–Schwarz gives |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
L(ζ) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I is continuous linear, with |L(ξ)|² = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).

Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).
